title: Associate ambulance practitioner
change: Occupational standard and assessment plan revised
overviewOfRole: Responding to 999 and urgent calls, and providing emergency care for people as part of an ambulance crew.
entryRequirements: <p class="MsoNormal">To enter an apprenticeship the minimum age of an AAP is 18 years. Entry requirements will be determined by the employer and the provider, and may include interview, assessment and fitness test. Entrants must hold a valid full UK driving licence, including licence categories required to legally drive the employer's vehicles.</p>
ssa2: 1.2 Nursing, and subjects and vocations allied to medicine

knowledges.detail: Legislation, local and national policies, protocols and codes of conduct or practice and ethics that apply to own role, including the implications of non-compliance.
Scope of practice and limitations of own competence.
Escalation and reporting processes for concerns and queries.
Principles of safeguarding and how to respond to safeguarding concerns in line with organisational protocols.
Strategies that develop resilience in self and others and where and how to access well-being support.
Principles of a duty of candour.
Techniques for managing challenging situations and reporting unsafe work practices.
Roles and responsibilities when responding to hazardous or major incidents, including public health emergencies.
Health inequalities, the contributing factors, and the impact on health and outcomes.
Principles of equality, diversity and inclusion, in respect to the care and treatment of service users.
Principles of person-centred care.
Valid and informed consent and the actions to take if this cannot be established.
Stepwise and holistic approaches to assessment of service users including history-taking and examination.
Human anatomy and physiology across the lifespan including, normal physiological parameters to support diagnosis.
Pathophysiology of a range of conditions across the lifespan, recognising variability in presentation and how to adapt the care plan to meet service user needs.
Safe and effective use of medicines and medical gases and the underpinning principles of pharmacology.
Medical, physical, trauma, mental health and socio-economic factors across the lifespan of service users.
How to regularly check and use equipment safely reporting defects.
Importance of safety netting prior to discharge, following organisational referral pathways.
Resuscitation methods across the age ranges.
Principles of end-of-life care plans, considerations and impacts on assessment and treatment plans.
Mental capacity and its impact on service users.
Principles of dementia, learning disabilities and neurodivergent differences on service users.
Principles of sustainability and how they apply to own role and workplace.
Digital tools and technologies relevant to own role and workplace.
Communication strategies and adaption methods to maximise understanding in the delivery of care.
Principles of confidentiality and how to use, record, store and share data and information in line with General Data Protection Regulations.
Methods for recording interactions with service users and the importance of justifying the resulting actions and assessment decisions.
Protocols for communicating with other teams, organisations and services.
Roles and responsibilities of other teams, organisations and services operating in the emergency and urgent care environment and the impact of working collaboratively.
Protocols for the handover of service users.
Safe practice techniques, dynamic risk assessments and risk management, to maintain own safety and that of others.
Conflict resolution strategies.
Techniques for safe moving and handling.
Human factor approaches underpinning patient safety and quality improvement.
Importance of continuing professional development.
Principles of reflective practice to develop professional knowledge, skills and performance.
Wider determinants of health, the impact of service user behaviours and lifestyle choices on health and well-being.
Importance of health promotion and its contribution to reducing health inequalities.
Road safety legislation, recognised system of vehicle control, advanced and high-speed driving techniques and codes of practice.
Exemptions and non-exemptions of road safety legislation and eligibility to claim exemptions when driving.
Vehicle safety checks to ensure vehicles are roadworthy and clean.

behaviours.detail: Respect the values and beliefs of service users, their families, carers and those you work with.
Show compassion and empathy for service users, their families, carers and those you work with.
Have the courage to challenge areas of concern.

skills.detail: Apply legislation, local and national policies, protocols and codes of conduct or practice and ethics.
Work within the scope of practice and the limitations of own competence.
Escalate and report to the senior clinician when needed.
Identify and respond to safeguarding concerns in line with organisational protocols.
Use resilience strategies to manage health and well-being of self and others, seeking help and support when necessary.
Respond to factors contributing to health inequalities, and the impact on health and outcomes.
Provide inclusive care and treatment to service users.
Provide and promote person-centred care.
Establish valid and informed consent and escalate if this cannot be established.
Conduct stepwise and holistic assessments including history-taking and examination.
Obtain physiological measurements and compare to physiological parameters to inform a working diagnosis.
Monitor and evaluate condition of service users and make changes or recommendations to the treatment plan.
Prepare and administer medicines and medical gases safely.
Deliver care to service users across the lifespan covering all medical, physical, trauma, mental health and socio-economic factors.
Select, check and safely use equipment and report defects.
Provide safety netting information prior to their discharge.
Safely perform resuscitation across age ranges.
Undertake diagnostic and functional assessment of mental capacity.
Deliver care to services users with dementia, learning disabilities and neurodivergent differences.
Manage resources using sustainable working practices.
Use digital tools and technologies relevant to own role and workplace.
Communicate using strategies and adapting these to maximise understanding in the delivery of care.
Use, record, store and share data and confidential information in line with General Data Protection Regulations.
Record interactions with service users and justify actions and assessment decisions.
Follow protocols when communicating with other teams, organisations and services.
Work collaboratively with other teams, organisations and services to facilitate team working in the emergency and urgent care environment.
Follow protocols for the handover of service users.
Establish safe environments for practice, using dynamic risk assessments which appropriately manage the risk and safety of self and others.
Use conflict resolution strategies.
Use safe moving and handling techniques.
Engage in and record continuing professional development.
Reflect on own practice to develop professional knowledge, skills and performance.
Act on opportunities to educate and empower service users to maximise their own health and well-being.
Use advanced driving skills to respond to emergency and routine calls and to safely transport service users in emergency and non-emergency driving conditions.
Apply exemptions to safely make progress when driving.
Carry out vehicle checks to ensure that the vehicle is roadworthy and clean.

qualifications.title: Level 3 Certificate in Emergency Response Ambulance Driving (RQF)
qualifications.anyAdditionalInformation: Level 3 Certificate in Emergency Response Ambulance Driving Qualification. This is an Ofqual qualification and is the only mandated qualification that meets regulatory requirements. Individuals would have to complete the Level 3 Certificate in Emergency Response Ambulance Driving Qualification unless they have already passed either the legacy Institute of Health Care Development (IHCD) Driver training programme or Chief Ambulance Officer approved internal programmes with a high-speed driving component where candidates can demonstrate current and relevant driving experience. Previous driver training programmes must meet the criteria set out by the Department for Transport for high-speed driving in the Road Safety Act.

duties.dutyDetail: Practise within the limits of own competence, scope of practice and responsibility following relevant legislation.
Practise in a non-discriminatory and inclusive manner recognising the impact of culture, equality and diversity.
Deliver care, drawing on relevant knowledge and skills to inform practice.
Communicate effectively maintaining confidentiality and records.
Work with others and as part of the team.
Establish and maintain a safe practice environment.
Maintain and further develop own knowledge and skills through continuing professional development activities.
Promote the health and well-being of service users, acting on opportunities to educate and empower service users to maximise their own health and well-being and prevent ill health.
Drive an ambulance or response vehicle under emergency and non-emergency driving conditions.
